gui.huhutalk.manual.huhutalk.what.title: HuhuTalk
gui.huhutalk.manual.huhutalk.what.body:
HuhuTalk is an add-on for Touhou Little Maid. Its main purpose is to fill the gap of not being able to chat with your maid remotely, and it gives the maid a chat style made for the phone UI, a new delivery route, and a privacy-mode toggle. Thanks for trying it out!

— This mod was built with AI assistance (I am not formally trained).
gui.huhutalk.manual.huhutalk.loading.bod: The mod uses loading tickets, so there is some extra performance cost. See the Items & Blocks section for details. So please use the Pro phone in moderation.
gui.huhutalk.manual.huhutalk.extra_cmd.b: On top of that, some extra commands were added (more may come later). You can use natural language to send the maid AI to a coordinate / stay at a coordinate / come to you, with formats like go somewhere and do something, or stay somewhere and do something (see Guide 8).
gui.huhutalk.manual.phone.draw_font.body:
The phone is drawn as an overlay.

The font size inside the phone follows the GUI scale you set, so feel free to pick the font ratio you like.

If you use a large GUI but want small text, or a small GUI but want large text, you can scale the font again on the desktop Settings app → Display & Rendering page — though some font rendering issues may appear. That page also holds the E-ink Screen switch, aspect ratio, phone size and brightness.
gui.huhutalk.manual.phone.keys.title: Control Keys (%1$s / %2$s)
gui.huhutalk.manual.phone.keys.body:
The phone is operated with your bound control keys. Left = %1$s, right = %2$s, scroll = hold %1$s and drag.
By default left confirms and right goes back one level (you can also tap the back button at the top left).
gui.huhutalk.manual.phone.emg_close.body: There is an invisible emergency close button (an X) at the right end of the top bar, for special situations. (See Fig. 1)
gui.huhutalk.manual.settings.entry.title: Where Settings Live
gui.huhutalk.manual.settings.entry.body:
Settings live inside HuhuTalk. Open HuhuTalk and switch to the rightmost option on the bottom navigation. HuhuTalk's bottom “Settings” manages the phone itself (messages, rescue, animation, colors and the HuhuTalk icon). The desktop “Settings” app manages vision, desktop icons, and the Display & Rendering page (E-ink screen, aspect ratio, phone size, font scale and brightness).

PS:
the mod is called huhutalk, and having just one lonely app felt odd, so I plan to add more apps later.
Even without a phone, you can press %1$s to bring up the standalone screen (it uses its own cursor; hold the status bar with a control key to drag it).

Its height can go up to the actual screen height and down to 1/2 of it (I did not consider very large screens for now). If you shrink it until the text no longer fits, the slider cannot be pinned — that is a small bug, but it prevents getting stuck, so it is a good bug. (Fig. 11)

Screen options moved:
aspect ratio, phone size, font scale and brightness now live on the desktop Settings app → Display & Rendering page.

Aspect ratio:
20:9, 9:16 and 4:3 are supported, and the internal UI adapts to the content.

E-ink Screen (off by default):
only affects the screen on the held phone model; the standalone floating screen is not affected by this toggle. When off, the phone screen is drawn after shader processing, keeping the interface's original colors and stable brightness. When on, it is drawn before shader processing and is handled by the shader pack, so the result varies by pack and may show ghosting or bloom. Without Iris or with shaders disabled, turning it on may make no visible difference. It does not change world lighting settings, does not simulate black-and-white or a low refresh rate, and is not a true e-ink simulation.

Top bar:
the phone's upper bar (showing time, battery and signal) is the drag handle for the standalone screen's position — move it wherever you like!

Brightness slider:
“Even a phone case can be dimmed.”

Phone case:
you can pick any full block from your inventory, though it may not look great.
gui.huhutalk.manual.settings.chat.title: Chat Settings
gui.huhutalk.manual.settings.chat.body:
Do Not Disturb:
turns off the red badge and the message sound; off by default.

Maid Whisper:
turns off the maid's AI bubble for a more private chat experience.

Immersive Chat:
while on, chats opened from the phone will not show the maid's replies in the lower-left chat HUD.
Because phone messages deliberately add typing delay, the lower-left HUD actually arrives first; this option is for a more immersive feel. (See Fig. 2)
gui.huhutalk.manual.settings.potion.body:
The maid's potion rescue is on by default and is independent of this narration toggle: if you die while carrying the Pro phone and a loaded maid wearing the phone has a healing potion in her backpack, she will throw it to you remotely 5 seconds after death and revive you to the health that potion restores. Falling into lava also gets an additional fire-resistance potion; falling into the void is not rescued.

This toggle only controls rescue-related AI narration. When off, the maid still registers the death, consumes the potion and revives you at the death point; she simply no longer calls the AI for the instant rescue report, the low-potion warning or the streak summary, so no tokens are spent. (See Fig. 3)
gui.huhutalk.manual.settings.supply.body: A special work mode: while in it, the maid tops up your low health/hunger. Leaving the mode also triggers the LLM; turn off the model dialogue with this option. (See Fig. 3)
gui.huhutalk.manual.settings.sos.title: SOS
gui.huhutalk.manual.settings.sos.body: On a maid's screen you can bind her as your SOS summon. In an emergency, press this button to call her over.
gui.huhutalk.manual.settings.anim.title: Screen & Message Animation
gui.huhutalk.manual.settings.anim.body:
Message Animation:
for extra realism, each maid message is split into sentences and gets a wind-up based on length (sending another line before she finishes makes her render it all at once).

Screen Animation:
this option controls screen transitions — “who doesn't want a pretty UI animation?” (See Fig. 4)
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.input.title: Input Box
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.input.body: Tap to start typing, press Esc to exit, press Enter to send.
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.toolbar.title: Bottom Toolbar
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.toolbar.body: From left to right: voice input, stickers, gallery, camera, and the attachment bar. (See Fig. 5)
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.voice.title: Voice Input
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.voice.body: Press %1$s by default to start; note that this input method does not trigger private chat! (Fig. 6)
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.sticker.title: Stickers
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.sticker.body: If you send a sticker, the maid will always reply with one — but it is not from the LLM (otherwise the tokens would burn up). You can of course ask her to send stickers back. (Fig. 7)
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.gallery.title: Gallery
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.gallery.body:
Only photos saved on the camera screen are stored here. You can send one image at a time, and can send an image together with text — but the maid only replies after the image has been recognized. (Fig. 8)

Note:
DeepSeek follows Touhou Little Maid's config by default; you can also choose and configure other vision platforms in the desktop “Settings” app. If you already put a DeepSeek API key in the original mod, image features work right away.

Note:
vision has fairly high latency, please be patient orz.
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.camera.title: Camera
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.camera.body:
Press %1$s to take a photo, hold %1$s to save, %2$s to exit.
Switch to the front camera for selfies: the preview is mirrored, and saving writes the photo in the normal orientation; retaking returns to the selfie view.
If you do not save, the confirmed image is only used for this send and is not stored locally. (Fig. 9)
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.file.title: Send Files
gui.huhutalk.manual.chat.file.body: Tap an item you want to send to select it into the pending bar; tap it there to cancel. Return to the chat page and tap send. (Fig. 10)
gui.huhutalk.manual.contacts.online.body: The maid is loaded and can talk.
gui.huhutalk.manual.contacts.offline.bod: The maid is in an unloaded chunk and cannot talk; find her with the red fox scroll.
gui.huhutalk.manual.contacts.shutdown.bo: The maid currently has no phone in her accessory slot. (Fig. 13)
gui.huhutalk.manual.contacts.settings.bo:
Set Avatar:
by default the maid gets a close-up portrait; more poses or using stickers as avatars may come later.

Delete Chat:
removes only HuhuTalk's add-on chat storage; the actual context still lives in the Touhou Little Maid mod.

Delete Contact:
if the maid dies by accident (cries), there has to be a way to remove her (sobs).
But if a contact was deleted only because she was lost (chunk not loaded), she will be re-added the next time she picks up her phone.

Bind SOS:
choose which maid to summon and in what mode (for different “unit types”); up to four maids can be your demon-lord guards. (Fig. 12)
gui.huhutalk.manual.navbar.signal.title: Signal Bar
gui.huhutalk.manual.navbar.signal.body: Bad dimensions add signal delay: 0.5s in the End, 1s in the Nether.
gui.huhutalk.manual.navbar.battery.title: Battery
gui.huhutalk.manual.commands.move.title: Move to / Wait for me
gui.huhutalk.manual.commands.move.body: The maid goes to the spot you indicate and waits; when you come near, she starts following you. A work mode can be attached.
gui.huhutalk.manual.commands.come.title: Come / To me
gui.huhutalk.manual.commands.come.body: The maid comes to your side: if close she walks over, if far she teleports.
gui.huhutalk.manual.commands.stay.title: Stay / Go stay
gui.huhutalk.manual.commands.stay.body: The maid goes to the spot you indicate. Home mode is on, so she will not follow you when you pass by.
gui.huhutalk.manual.compat.journeymap.bo:
Compatible with JourneyMap.
You can use natural language to send the maid to a waypoint to work, e.g. “go to Happy Home and harvest the crops.” “go to the slime ranch and wait for me.”
gui.huhutalk.manual.items.watch.title: Phone Watch
gui.huhutalk.manual.items.watch.body:
A cheaper phone, but it has no data card, so it must be used together with the WiFi Block.
A maid holding a Phone Watch within its three-chunk-wide coverage area stays force-loaded and is given loading tickets. (Fig. 15)
gui.huhutalk.manual.items.wifi_block.bod:
An energy-saving design for this mod: to avoid the performance cost of many maids gathering and each receiving forced loading tickets, it issues no loading tickets to nearby chunks when no Phone Watch maid is around, so there is no performance cost.
If and only if a watch-holding maid is nearby does it force-load the chunk she is in. (Fig. 16)
gui.huhutalk.manual.items.pro_phone.body: Continuously issues forced-loading tickets for your maid, but to protect performance it only loads one chunk — so if your maid is the Flash, she may run into unloaded chunks. (Fig. 17)
gui.huhutalk.manual.outro.final.title: In Short!
gui.huhutalk.manual.outro.final.body:
This mod was developed by me (Luochun) with the help of an AI workflow. If you find any bugs or have suggestions, please write to Anirtual@gmail.com — thank you!
And — thanks for downloading and trying it, I love you all!

fml.menu.mods.info.description.huhutalk:
Huhutalk is an add-on mod for Touhou Little Maid.

It fills the gap that maids could not chat remotely, adding a phone-UI-exclusive chat style, a new message reception path, and a privacy-mode toggle.
You can stay in touch with your maid anytime through the phone, and can use natural language to order her to a specific coordinate, stay put, or come back to you (move to / come / stay).

This mod was developed by Luochun with the help of an AI workflow. Thanks for downloading and playing!
